definitions.explanation: The single continuous filament a silkworm spins to make its cocoon, the raw material of silk thread. A term from sericulture and the silk industry.

examples.japanese: ⟦{繭|まゆ}→繭：13861_mayu⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{繭糸|けんし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}り{出|だ}す→取り出す：04220_toridasu⟧。
examples.english: To extract silk thread from cocoons.

examples.japanese: {繭糸|けんし}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{品質|ひんしつ}→品質：09507_hinshitsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{蚕|かいこ}→蚕：21218_kaiko⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{育|そだ}て→育てる：01235_sodateru⟧⟦{方|かた}→方：10665_kata⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{変|か}わる→変わる：00714_kawaru⟧。
examples.english: The quality of silk thread changes depending on how the silkworms are raised.

examples.japanese: ⟦{一|ひと}つ→一つ：02948_hitotsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{繭|まゆ}→繭：13861_mayu⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{取|と}れる→取れる：02376_toreru⟧{繭糸|けんし}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{長|なが}さ→長さ：05326_nagasa⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧1,000⟦メートル→メートル：02975_meetoru⟧⟦{以上|いじょう}→以上：01308_ijou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: The filament from a single cocoon can be more than 1,000 meters long.

notes:
Composed of {繭|けん} (cocoon) and {糸|し} (thread). Japan has a long history of sericulture (⟦{養蚕|ようさん}→養蚕：27720_yousan⟧), and silk production was a major industry from the Edo period through the early twentieth century. The {富岡|とみおか}{製糸場|せいしじょう} (Tomioka Silk Mill), a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is a famous example of Japan's silk industry.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{繭|まゆ}→繭：13861_mayu⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{繭糸|けんし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}る→取る：00565_toru⟧: to reel the filament from cocoons
- {繭糸|けんし}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{品質|ひんしつ}→品質：09507_hinshitsu⟧: filament quality

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{生糸|きいと}→生糸：27719_kiito⟧: raw silk, the thread made by reeling several cocoon filaments together; {繭糸|けんし} is the single filament.
- ⟦{絹糸|きぬいと}→絹糸：27626_kinuito⟧: silk thread — processed silk thread ready for weaving
- ⟦{絹|きぬ}→絹：01383_kinu⟧: silk — the finished fabric material
